newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND MOVE CLOSER TO VICTORY IN CLASH OF TOP TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND MOVE CLOSER TO VICTORY IN CLASH OF TOP TEAMS.

text.p: Queensland moved towards a likely victory against Western Australia on the third day of a match involving the top two sides in the Sheffield Shield competition on Saturday.
The home team reduced Western Australia to 96 for four in their second innings, still needing another 313 runs to win, at close of play at the Gabba in Brisbane.
Queensland earlier set a target by scoring 412 all out in their second innings, an overall lead of 408.

On a wicket providing variable bounce, Western Australia, who lead the Shield table by six points from Queensland and New South Wales, will be looking to all-rounder and captain Tom Moody, their last remaining recognised batsman, when play resumes.
In Melbourne, Victoria made a bold start in the run chase against New South Wales.
Australia test opener Matthew Elliott and Graeme Vimpani added 136 runs in an unbroken opening stand, leaving the home side with another 255 runs to score to pull off an unlikely win.
At close of play on the third day, Vimpani remained unbeaten on 77 alongside Elliott, who was 54 not out.
Victoria were set a target of 391 for victory after New South Wales declared their second innings on 264 for eight.
In Adelaide, South Australia reached 287 for eight at close of play on the first day of their match against Tasmania.
